title: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star
description: A nursery rhyme that makes a perfect first tune: six white keys, mostly moving one step at a time.

steps.title: An old French tune
steps.description: The melody is older than the words. It comes from an 18th-century French song, "Ah! vous dirai-je, maman", and Mozart wrote a famous set of variations on it. It's also the tune of the alphabet song and "Baa, Baa, Black Sheep". We're in C major and only need six notes, C up to A. Start with your thumb on middle C.

steps.title: Phrase 1: "Twinkle, twinkle"
steps.description: Play middle C twice, then jump up to G and play that twice. That jump is what makes the opening sound so bright.
steps.hint: G is five white keys up if you count C as one: C, D, E, F, G. Your little finger should be right on it.

steps.title: Phrase 2: "Little star"
steps.description: Step up to A for "lit-tle", then come back to G for "star". G ends the phrase, so let it ring a little longer.
steps.hint: A is the white key just above G. Play it twice, then come back down to G.

steps.title: Phrase 3: "How I wonder what you are"
steps.description: Now walk all the way back down to where you started, two of each: F F, E E, D D, then one C. Think of it as going down a staircase, two taps on every step.
steps.hint: Each pair is one white key lower than the last. You finish back on middle C.

steps.title: Middle: "Up above the world so high"
steps.description: The middle part starts back up on G and walks down the same way: G G, F F, E E, D. It stops on D instead of C, so it feels like it's leading somewhere. The next line, "like a diamond in the sky", uses exactly the same notes.
steps.hint: Same staircase as before, just starting higher and stopping one step early.

steps.title: The C major chord
steps.description: Now some chords to go under the tune. C major is the home chord, the one the song starts and ends on. Play C, E and G together.
steps.hint: Thumb on C, middle finger on E, little finger on G. Any octave works.

steps.title: The F major chord
steps.description: F major goes under "lit-tle" and "how I", where the melody sits on A and then F. Play F, A and C.
steps.hint: Same shape as C, moved up: F, skip a key, A, skip a key, C.

steps.title: The G major chord
steps.description: G major comes in under "what you", just before the melody lands back on C for "are". It's the chord that pulls you home. Play G, B and D.
steps.hint: Same shape again, starting on G: G, B, D.

steps.title: That's the tune
steps.description: You've got the melody and the three chords that go with it: C, F and G, or I, IV and V in this key. Those three show up in a huge number of songs. Try playing the whole melody from memory, then see if you can hold the chords in your left hand underneath it.

steps.title: Which chords?
steps.description: Which three chords did you use to go with the melody?
